heard: Voyager traveled 4 billion miles to look back at us. Astronomer Carl Sagan first proposed the photo in 1981. NASA rejected it for years, fearing the sun would blind the cameras. NASA finally took the shot in 1990 from deep space. Then, Voyager shut down its cameras for the last time. Our entire world appeared as 0.12 pixels. Without a lucky sunbeam, the planet would be totally invisible. The photo explains why Voyager traveled 4 billion miles to look back at us.
